title: Ungate the primitive IR: MetalPrimitive -> GpuPrimitive, drop macOS cfg
description:
Make the retained-mode display list backend-neutral. This is the single
highest-leverage step in the port and it unblocks nearly everything else.

The types are ALREADY platform-free data - they are just cfg-gated and
named "Metal". In crates/eseqlisp/src/widget_render/mod.rs:
  :538  WidgetInstance          (#[repr(C)], f32 arrays only)
  :558  WidgetViewport
  :585  MetalRectPrimitive
  :600  MetalQuadPrimitive
  :619  MetalProportionalTextPrimitive
  :754  MetalPrimitive          (the enum)
  :788  MetalPrimitiveRun
  :799  MetalPrimitiveRunKey
  :806  MetalPrimitiveRunIndex
  :814  RetainedMetalPrimitiveRunStats
  :4283 ndc_bounds()
plus metal_widget_instance(), drain_overlay_primitives(),
collect_metal_primitive_runs_recursive(), push_overlay_primitive() (:358).

Scope:
- Remove #[cfg(target_os = "macos")] from these definitions and from the
  ~30 widget_render/*.rs modules that import them from `super`.
- Rename Metal* -> Gpu* (GpuPrimitive, GpuRectPrimitive, GpuPrimitiveRun,
  ...). Mechanical but touches many files; do it in the same change so the
  naming does not stay misleading for the rest of the port.
- Leave ui/metal_backend.rs consuming the renamed types unchanged in behavior.

There are 630 cfg(target_os="macos") occurrences in crates/eseqlisp/src.
The heaviest files are widget_render/mod.rs (98), patcher/render.rs (87),
patcher/tests.rs (49), editor/tests.rs (48), knob_number.rs (43),
timeline.rs (33). Most should disappear with this change; the residue is
the genuine Metal/CoreText/objc code plus the shader-string trait method
(handled in the next bead).

Note: number_picker.rs also fails on E0407 `metal_fragment_shader is not a
member of trait WidgetDefinition` and on BUTTON_SURFACE_SHADER /
NUMBER_PICKER_TRI_SHADER consts. Those are MSL strings, not data - they are
the next bead's problem. Either land them together or stub the trait method
temporarily.
acceptance_criteria: cargo check -p eseqlisp --lib succeeds on Linux with zero errors; macOS build and test suite unchanged
close_reason: Reviewed. cargo check -p eseqlisp --lib is error-free on Linux (31 errors at f6507433~1); --all-targets also clean. macOS proven unchanged: normalizing the Metal*->Gpu* renames and stripping #[cfg(target_os="macos")] lines makes every changed file byte-identical to f6507433~1. Review fixes in 9354350d: stale collect_metal_primitive_runs/build_metal_primitive_run_index in sequencer tests (broke the macOS test build), refresh_metal_* -> refresh_gpu_*, four over-ungated sites re-gated, and a caret-clamp panic the ungating unmasked. Follow-ups filed: eseq-linux.14, notes on .12 and .2.

title: [macOS host] Capture and commit the three-way glyph golden set (CoreText@mac, fontdue@mac, fontdue@linux)
description:
REQUIRES A MACOS MACHINE. This is the only bead in the glyph-atlas chain that
does. Everything downstream becomes a Linux-runnable numeric/pixel diff once
this lands.

HANDOFF (agreed with user 2026-08-23): the worker pushes the `eseq-linux`
branch -- it currently has NO upstream configured -- and the user pulls it on
the Mac and runs the harness there. This bead is a RUN-AND-COMMIT bead, not a
design bead; eseq-linux.23 does the engineering so this session is short.

CAPTURE THREE POINTS, NOT TWO. The obvious comparison (CoreText vs Linux
fontdue) confounds two independent changes: the rasterizer changed AND the
platform/font-availability changed. Capture all three so they separate:

  1. coretext-macos    -- checkout 57b76e2a^ in a scratch worktree, apply the
                          eseq-linux.23 harness on top, run.
                          This is the ONLY way to get CoreText numbers: 57b76e2a
                          deleted the CoreText atlas outright and dropped
                          objc2-core-text from Cargo.toml.
  2. fontdue-macos     -- checkout the branch HEAD, run the harness unmodified.
  3. fontdue-linux     -- already producible on the Linux host; the worker
                          generates this one, not you.

Point 2 is the one people skip and it is the most diagnostically useful: a
delta between 1 and 2 is purely the rasterizer swap, and a delta between 2 and
3 is purely the platform (font selection, DPI, scale). Reading only 1-vs-3
will send someone chasing the wrong cause. Note that eseq-linux.19 already
found load_system_ui_font picking a condensed face (NimbusSansNarrow) on
Linux -- that is exactly a 2-vs-3 class problem, and if it is still open when
this runs, expect it to show up in the deltas and say so in the notes rather
than treating it as rasterizer error.

COMMIT: the metrics JSON and PNGs for points 1 and 2, under the
crates/eseqlisp/tests/fixtures/ subdirectory eseq-linux.23 establishes.
Record in the bead notes: macOS version, hardware/chip, display scale factor,
and the exact commit each capture came from. Without those the goldens are
not reproducible and will rot silently.

DO NOT judge the deltas here -- just produce and commit the reference data.
Interpreting them and deciding whether they are acceptable is eseq-linux.20,
which is Linux-runnable once these files exist.
acceptance_criteria: coretext-macos and fontdue-macos metrics JSON + PNGs are committed under the fixtures subdirectory from eseq-linux.23; each capture records its source commit, macOS version, chip, and display scale factor in the bead notes; the CoreText set is confirmed captured from 57b76e2a^ (pre-swap); no delta interpretation or sign-off is done in this bead
notes: Blocked on a macOS host by design; this is the single Mac-dependent step. User confirmed 2026-08-23 they can pull a pushed branch and run captures on a Mac. NOTE: branch 'eseq-linux' has no upstream configured yet -- it must be pushed before this bead can start.

title: Deterministic font metrics + text capture harness (must also run at 57b76e2a^ for the CoreText reference)
description:
Linux-doable NOW. This is the harness half of the eseq-linux.20 acceptance
check, split out so a Linux-only worker can build it without a Mac.

WHY THIS SHAPE: CoreText is completely gone from the tree. 57b76e2a
("feat(eseqlisp): replace CoreText glyph atlas") rewrote glyph_atlas.rs
wholesale (1186 lines changed) and dropped objc2-core-text from
crates/eseqlisp/Cargo.toml. Only a stale comment at
widget_render/patcher/display.rs:310 mentions CoreText now. So the CoreText
reference can ONLY be produced by checking out 57b76e2a^ and running a
harness there. Git history is immutable, so nothing is at risk of being lost
-- but the harness has to be built to reach back.

THE HARNESS CONTRACT IS THE OUTPUT SCHEMA, NOT A SINGLE CODE PATH.
At 57b76e2a^ the atlas is CoreText-backed with a different internal API than
HEAD's fontdb/fontdue one. Do not try to write one file that compiles
unmodified at both commits. Instead:
  - define a stable, versioned output schema (JSON + PNG naming)
  - keep the harness a standalone bin/example with a THIN adapter over
    whatever the atlas exposes at that commit
  - keep the adapter small enough that applying the harness onto 57b76e2a^
    is a cherry-pick plus a short shim, not a port
Verify this by actually doing it: check out 57b76e2a^ in a scratch worktree
and confirm the harness builds and runs there on Linux. It will produce
garbage-or-error for the CoreText path on Linux (that is fine and expected --
CoreText cannot run here); what you are proving is that the harness COMPILES
and its non-CoreText plumbing works, so the Mac session is a run, not a
debugging session.

METRICS OUTPUT (JSON, diffs cleanly in git -- stable key order, fixed float
formatting, no timestamps, no absolute paths, no hostname):
  for each (font_size, scale_factor) in a FIXED list covering the real sizes
  and scales the UI uses:
    cell_w, cell_h, ascent, descent, leading
  plus per-glyph advance_width for a fixed charset (at minimum the ASCII
  printable range; 'm' specifically, since cell_w derives from it).
Cover the SizedFontCache proportional sizes too, not just the mono grid --
eseq-linux.20 calls out ascent/descent/leading for every proportional size.

SCREENSHOT OUTPUT (PNG):
  render ONE fixed, checked-in text buffer -- same content, same size, same
  scale, same theme -- and write a deterministic PNG. No clock, no random,
  no project state. Two runs on the same host must be byte-identical.

OUTPUT LOCATION: crates/eseqlisp/tests/fixtures/ is the existing convention
(currently holds module-alias-migration). Put goldens under a new
subdirectory there, named by <rasterizer>-<os>-<arch> so the three-way set in
the follow-up bead lands side by side without collisions.

DO NOT capture or commit any golden data in this bead. This bead builds and
proves the harness only; eseq-linux.24 runs it on macOS and commits the
reference set.
acceptance_criteria: A standalone harness emits the metrics JSON and the deterministic PNG on Linux; two consecutive runs on the same host are byte-identical; the JSON schema is stable/diffable (ordered keys, fixed float format, no timestamps/paths/hostnames); the fixed font-size x scale-factor list covers both the mono grid and the SizedFontCache proportional sizes; the harness is demonstrated to build and run in a scratch worktree at 57b76e2a^ (CoreText path may fail at runtime on Linux -- compiling and running there is what is being proven); no golden data is committed by this bead
notes: Split out of eseq-linux.20 on 2026-08-23 after the implementing worker correctly refused to fabricate macOS metrics/screenshots on a Linux host. Design decision (user, 2026-08-23): commit PNGs + metrics JSON to the repo; a macOS session is available on request via branch push/pull.

title: Judge the fontdue-vs-CoreText deltas against the committed goldens and sign off
description:
Carried over from eseq-linux.6, whose acceptance could not be run on the Linux
host that implemented 57b76e2a. RESTRUCTURED 2026-08-23: this bead no longer
requires a macOS machine. eseq-linux.23 builds the harness and eseq-linux.24
captures and commits the macOS reference data; this bead is now a pure diff
and judgement pass that runs on Linux.

The swap from CoreText to fontdb/fontdue changes layout-critical numbers and
appearance in ways that will not fail loudly:

  - cell_w: CTFont advances_for_glyphs('m') -> fontdue rasterize('m').advance_width
  - cell_h: CTFont ascent/descent/leading -> fontdue horizontal_line_metrics
    (hhea vs whatever CoreText reports)
  - SizedFontCache ascent/descent/leading for every proportional size
  - fontdue does no hinting and emits linear coverage; CoreText applies font
    smoothing and gamma, so glyphs will read thinner
  - copy_glyph_into_line rounds dst_y to whole rows, so vertical placement is
    integer-quantised where CoreText positioned subpixel

ATTRIBUTE EACH DELTA, DO NOT JUST MEASURE IT. The goldens are a three-way set
precisely so cause is separable:
    coretext-macos vs fontdue-macos  = the rasterizer swap, nothing else
    fontdue-macos   vs fontdue-linux = the platform, nothing else
A 1-vs-3 number alone conflates them and will send someone tuning the
rasterizer for what is actually a font-selection bug. eseq-linux.19
(load_system_ui_font picks condensed NimbusSansNarrow on Linux) is a known
2-vs-3 contributor -- if it is still open, expect it in the deltas and label
it as such rather than charging it to fontdue.

Note one pre-existing inconsistency the rewrite already FIXED, so do not read
it as a regression: old SizedFontCache::new seeded line_metrics under key
(base_font_size*10) using a font built at base_font_size WITHOUT the scale
multiplier, while sized_font() for the same key would have used size*scale.
The new cache has no seed and is self-consistent.

"Bounded" is not defined anywhere yet -- part of this bead is choosing the
threshold and writing down why. A sub-pixel cell_w drift is cosmetic; a
whole-pixel cell_h drift reflows the entire UI grid, because the grid lays
out on these numbers (WidgetViewport.cell_w/cell_h, metal_backend.rs:7629
text_cell_w/h, :7721, :7974). Treat those two cases differently.
acceptance_criteria: Runs on Linux against the committed goldens from eseq-linux.24 -- no macOS host required. cell_w/cell_h/ascent/descent/leading deltas computed for all three points (coretext-macos, fontdue-macos, fontdue-linux) at every captured font size and scale; each delta attributed to rasterizer swap (1-vs-2) or platform (2-vs-3); a bounded threshold is chosen and written down with its rationale; PNG diffs reviewed and any visible regression either fixed or filed as a new bead; sign-off recorded in the bead notes
notes:
Attempted 2026-08-23 from host omarchy, but this session is Linux (Linux 7.1.8-arch1-3 x86_64). The acceptance criteria require executing CoreText and Metal and visually inspecting macOS screenshots; neither can run or be meaningfully emulated on this host. No repository workaround or fabricated metrics/screenshots were introduced. Bead remains in progress and is not labeled needs-review because acceptance is incomplete.
Host-blocked, not work-blocked: acceptance requires executing CoreText + Metal and eyeballing macOS captures; the implementing agent runs on Linux (omarchy, Linux 7.1.8-arch1-3 x86_64). Deferred out of bd ready so the single-threaded worker stops re-picking it. The worker correctly refused to fabricate metrics or screenshots. Unblocked by the golden-capture route: see the new harness/reference beads.

title: Glyph atlas has no font fallback: a missing exact font name kills all text rendering
description:
Regression introduced by 57b76e2a (eseq-linux.6). glyph_atlas::load_named_font() resolves by exact PostScript name, then by exact family name, and returns None if neither hits. GlyphAtlas::new() propagates that None, so MetalBackend::self.atlas / self.text_atlas become None.

Downstream that is fatal, not cosmetic: metal_backend.rs:3913, :5006, :5363, :5943, :5994 do self.atlas.as_mut().ok_or(BackendError::MetalError)?, and :3860 / :4817 bail out of the frame entirely. mono cell_w/cell_h also come from the atlas (:3752-3784), so layout collapses too.

The old CoreText path could not fail this way: CTFont::with_name() always returns a font, silently substituting the system font, and the code only logged a warning.

Reproduced on this Linux box (JetBrains Mono Nerd Font installed at /usr/share/fonts/TTF):
  GlyphAtlas::new("JetBrainsMono-Regular", 13.0) -> None
  GlyphAtlas::new("JetBrains Mono Nerd Font", 13.0) -> Some (PS name JetBrainsMonoNF-Regular)
The hardcoded name at metal_backend.rs:3774 and :6119/:6129 is "JetBrainsMono-Regular", so any machine carrying the Nerd Font variant (or no JetBrains Mono at all) gets a dead UI.
acceptance_criteria: load_named_font falls back through a monospace preference list and finally Family::Monospace so it can only fail when the machine has no font at all; a test asserts GlyphAtlas::new with a deliberately bogus font name still returns Some
close_reason: Fallback chain verified: exact name -> normalized family stem -> monospace preference list -> Family::Monospace -> any monospaced face -> any face. Reviewer added the stem match and the two last-resort steps (cb7a9a24 alone could still return None on a box without a fontconfig monospace alias, and picked Liberation Mono over the reporting machine's own JetBrainsMono Nerd Font). 7 glyph_atlas tests pass; the 41 other eseqlisp lib failures reproduce identically at clean HEAD (dgen toolchain exec-format + /tmp collisions).

title: Cross-platform glyph atlas: replace CoreText (layout-critical, top risk)
description:
TOP RISK OF THE WHOLE PORT. crates/eseqlisp/src/ui/glyph_atlas.rs is 554
lines of CoreText with no non-macOS path at all (cfg gates at :9 and :553).

What it does: CTFont::with_name, CGBitmapContextCreate, rasterizes glyphs
into a shared R8Unorm atlas packed with etagere, plus SizedFontCache (:242)
for line metrics and a separate ProportionalGlyphAtlas.

Why it is the risk: it is load-bearing for LAYOUT, not just drawing.
  :84  cell_w derived from font.advances_for_glyphs()
  :81  cell_h = ceil(ascent + descent + leading)
and the entire UI grid lays out on those - see WidgetViewport.cell_w/cell_h
and ui/metal_backend.rs:7629 (text_cell_w/h), :7721, :7974. Swap the
rasterizer and the whole interface shifts. This will NOT fail loudly; it
will look subtly wrong everywhere (metrics, hinting, gamma).

Options, roughly in order of completeness vs weight:
  - cosmic-text: shaping + font fallback + layout. Heaviest, most complete.
  - swash (raster) + fontdue/ab_glyph: lighter, you own layout.
Whatever is chosen must also serve the ProportionalText primitive, not just
the monospace grid.

Also note the CoreText Y-up convention baked into the atlas (:6, :33, :186)
- v is stored Y-up and flipped in the shader. Pick a convention and make it
explicit rather than inheriting CoreText's by accident.

Suggested approach: build a metrics comparison harness first. Render the
same buffer through CoreText and the candidate rasterizer, diff cell_w/cell_h
/ascent/descent and a few full screenshots, BEFORE committing to a library.
acceptance_criteria: Glyph and proportional atlases build on Linux; metrics harness shows cell_w/cell_h/ascent/descent deltas vs CoreText are understood and bounded; screenshots of the same buffer compared side by side
notes:
Reviewed 2026-08-23 against commit 57b76e2a.

Verified on this Linux host:
- cargo test -p eseqlisp --lib glyph_atlas: 2 passed (cpu_atlases_measure_and_rasterize_on_every_platform, atlas_uvs_follow_top_down_bitmap_rows)
- cargo check -p eseqlisp --features wgpu --all-targets: clean
- cargo check -p eseqlisp --target x86_64-apple-darwin --all-targets: clean (only a pre-existing unused-import warning in editor/widget_focus.rs:1170)
- no CoreText/CTFont/CGBitmapContext references remain in crates/

Correctness confirmed by reading: the Y convention is right. The old doc comment claiming a v = 1.0 - v shader flip was stale - neither the old MSL (text frag sampled in.uv directly) nor the old vertex emission flipped anything. CGBitmapContext memory rows are top-down, so drawing at CG y=descent already put the baseline at memory row cell_h-descent. The new code reproduces exactly that with baseline = cell_h - descent and top-down fontdue output, and the vertex emission at metal_backend.rs:7383-7400 is byte-identical to before. Proportional offset_x replacing the hardcoded -2.0*scale padding is a genuine fix for overhanging glyphs.

Findings filed: eseq-linux.18 (P1, no font fallback - reproduced), eseq-linux.19 (P2, condensed Linux UI font - reproduced), eseq-linux.20 (P1, the macOS metrics/screenshot acceptance check this bead could not run), eseq-linux.21 (P3, font reparse per zoom step), eseq-linux.22 (P3, dead deps and cleanup).
close_reason: Implementation reviewed and accepted. CoreText is gone, the portable fontdb/fontdue atlas builds and rasterizes on Linux, the Y convention is correct and explicit, and both Linux and x86_64-apple-darwin compile clean. Remaining work split out: eseq-linux.18/.19 (confirmed bugs), eseq-linux.20 (the macOS metrics+screenshot acceptance check, which no Linux host can run), eseq-linux.21/.22 (perf and cleanup).

title: wgpu backend skeleton: window, pipelines, rect/quad/clip from GpuPrimitive runs
description:
Stand up crates/eseqlisp/src/ui/wgpu_backend.rs as a third render target
beside ui/tui.rs and ui/metal_backend.rs, consuming the same GpuPrimitive
runs (see eseq-linux.1).

Scope for THIS bead: device/queue/surface setup, swapchain, one instanced
rect/quad pipeline, scissor rect (PushClipRect/PopClipRect), and the
primitive-run walk. Get a window on Linux drawing colored rectangles from a
real eseq widget tree. Text and the exotic pipelines are separate beads.

Sizing note: ui/metal_backend.rs is 10,954 lines but only ~280 touch
MTL*/objc2/Retained (156 of them in the Backend region :2260-7589, 37 in the
quad builder :7589-9984). The rest is instance-buffer and geometry building
that should be shared, not reimplemented. Factor that shared code out of
metal_backend.rs as you go rather than copying it.

Primitive variants to eventually cover (widget_render/mod.rs:754):
  ZLayer Rect ForegroundRect Quad Triangle GlyphRun ProportionalText
  PatchCable Circle Waveform Wavetable LiveSpectrogram Image WidgetInstance
  PushClipRect PopClipRect

Keep the retained-run cache working - WIDGET_PRIMITIVE_CACHE (:245),
MetalPrimitiveRunIndex (:806), RetainedMetalPrimitiveRunStats (:814). It
matters much more on a weak iGPU than on Apple silicon (see eseq-linux.12).

Decision already taken: add wgpu as a genuine third target. Do NOT collapse
the Metal backend into wgpu even though wgpu runs on Metal - that would
regress a tuned renderer. Revisit only after the Linux target is at parity.
acceptance_criteria: On Linux, a real eseq widget tree renders rects/quads with correct clipping and colors; shared geometry code factored out of metal_backend.rs rather than duplicated
close_reason: Reviewed. Fixed in 10c0e912: the spike tree emitted no rect/quad geometry (every box became an SDF WidgetInstance) so nothing painted; sRGB surface format washed colors out vs Metal's BGRA8Unorm; ZLayer z-ordering was dropped. Added an offscreen render+readback test that renders a production widget tree and asserts unshifted colors inside the clip and scissoring of the overhang - both assertions mutation-checked. Metal-side scissor duplication filed as eseq-linux.17.

title: WgslEmitter in sdf_codegen.rs: compile the SDF DSL to WGSL
description:
crates/eseqlisp/src/lang/sdf_codegen.rs (1858 LOC) compiles the eseqlisp SDF
DSL to Metal Shading Language via `struct MetalEmitter` (:24). Add a WGSL
emitter beside it so all user-authored shaders in content/*.lisp port for
free - no content changes at all.

Entry points to parallel:
  :1188 compile_sdf_to_metal
  :1192 compile_sdf_to_metal_with_state
  :1285 compile_sdf_expr
  :1289 compile_sdf_expr_with_theme
  :1069 SdfShaderOutput
  :1074 metal_safe_symbol
  :1078 uniform_layout
  :1090 emit_uniform_declarations
  :1023 expr_returns_float4

Most of the emitter is expression-level and type names appear in ~61 places
(float2/float3/float4). Consider extracting a small Emitter trait over type
names + statement forms rather than forking the file.

Real divergences to handle, not just renames:
- Types: float4 -> vec4<f32>, float2 -> vec2<f32>, float3 -> vec3<f32>
- Statements: `float4 x = expr;` -> `let x = expr;` / `var x = expr;`
  (the emitter pushes raw C-style decls, e.g. :263, :271, :337, :341, :348)
- WGSL has NO implicit numeric conversions. MSL happily mixes int/float
  literals; WGSL will reject. Audit format_float (:1008) and every literal
  site.
- Uniform declarations and binding model differ substantially
  (emit_uniform_declarations, uniform_layout).
- Function/entry-point syntax and attribute syntax.

Test strategy: golden tests that run BOTH emitters over the full content/
shader corpus (content/ui/materials.lisp, sequencer.lisp, step-grid.lisp,
legacy/mixer.lisp, browser.lisp, transport.lisp, sound-palette.lisp,
effects/*.lisp - 17 lisp files reference shaders). Assert the WGSL compiles
via naga. Snapshot both outputs so MSL cannot regress.
acceptance_criteria: Every shader in the content/ corpus emits WGSL that naga accepts; MSL output byte-identical to before (snapshot); golden tests cover both emitters
close_reason: Reviewed: MSL golden hash independently reproduced from the pre-WGSL emitter at 7f580a54 (63/63 corpus shaders, byte-identical); all 63 shaders emit WGSL that naga 24 parses and validates; corpus discovery verified complete (63 defwidgets in content/, 63 compiled). Fixed one defect in 6a5fb546: the golden test raced the process-global theme and failed under a full cargo test run.

title: Make WidgetDefinition shader source backend-tagged (MSL + WGSL coexist)
description:

WidgetDefinition trait, returning MSL source as a &str. Generalize so MSL
and WGSL can coexist and a backend picks its own.

Proposed shape: `fn fragment_shader(&self, backend: ShaderBackend) -> Option<&str>`
with ShaderBackend::{Msl, Wgsl}, or two separate methods. Prefer whichever
keeps the 25 call sites cheap to migrate.

Implementors (crates/eseqlisp/src/widget_render/):
  box_widget knob number_picker scroll timeline knob_number hslider matrix
  mod sound_glyph phaser_notch response_curve_editor modulator_curve
  multiband_meter roar_shaper toggle tree text_input vslider button
  adsr_editor dropdown roar_filter

Also generalize the free-standing shader consts that widgets reference
across module boundaries, e.g. button::BUTTON_SURFACE_SHADER and
NUMBER_PICKER_TRI_SHADER in number_picker.rs.

This bead only moves the plumbing. Actual WGSL bodies land in the
"port 25 widget fragment shaders" bead.
acceptance_criteria: Both backends can request shader source for any widget; macOS renders identically to before

title: Linux port: wgpu graphics target, cross-platform text, portable dgen host
description:
Port eseq to Linux. Three dependency clusters: graphics (Metal -> wgpu),
text (CoreText -> cross-platform rasterizer), and dgen/audio host
(Accelerate + Mach-O + CoreAudio assumptions).

KEY ARCHITECTURAL FINDING (scoping pass 2026-08-22):
`MetalPrimitive` is not Metal. widget_render/mod.rs:754 defines it, and it
plus WidgetInstance (:538), WidgetViewport (:558), MetalRectPrimitive
(:585), MetalProportionalTextPrimitive (:619) and ndc_bounds (:4283) are
plain #[repr(C)] data - f32 arrays, Rect, Color, String. Zero objc. They
are only cfg(target_os="macos")-gated and misleadingly named. eseq already
has a backend-neutral retained-mode display list.

Evidence: `cargo check -p eseqlisp --lib` on Linux yields 31 errors and
EVERY one is "cannot find MetalPrimitive/WidgetInstance/WidgetViewport/
ndc_bounds in super" - the cfg gate, not a real platform dependency.
Ungating them makes ~100k LOC of widget_render/ compile on Linux.

Corollary: ui/metal_backend.rs is 10,954 lines but only ~280 touch
MTL*/objc2/Retained. The other 97% is instance-buffer and geometry
building that is already API-agnostic.

Shader work splits in two:
- GENERATED (free): content/*.lisp authors SDF shaders in eseqlisp
  (defwidget :shader, material, lighting - see content/ui/materials.lisp).
  lang/sdf_codegen.rs (1858 LOC) compiles them to MSL via a MetalEmitter
  struct (:24). User content needs zero porting; add a WgslEmitter beside it.
- HAND-WRITTEN (the grind): ~3,300 lines of MSL in Rust string literals.
  1,149 in ui/metal_backend.rs (8 pipelines) and ~2,165 across 25 widgets'
  metal_fragment_shader() trait methods.

TOP RISK: text. ui/glyph_atlas.rs is 554 lines of CoreText with no non-mac
path, and it is load-bearing for LAYOUT not just drawing - cell_w comes from
font.advances_for_glyphs(), cell_h from ascent+descent+leading, and the whole
UI grid is laid out on those. A different rasterizer shifts the entire
interface. It will not fail loudly, it will look subtly wrong everywhere.

FREE WINS: no MIDI anywhere (no CoreMIDI, no midir). No NSOpenPanel/
NSSavePanel. AppKit surface in metal_backend.rs is only NSView (CAMetalLayer
attach), NSColor, NSAppearance (dark mode), NSHapticFeedback. winit 0.29 is
already a dependency, just sitting inside the macOS-only dep block.

STRATEGY: add wgpu as a genuine third target beside TUI and Metal. Do not
collapse Metal into wgpu - that would regress a tuned renderer. Revisit later.

title: [macOS host] Whole-frame Metal reference captures + sign off the wgpu shader ports
description:
REQUIRES A MACOS MACHINE. Mirrors eseq-linux.24, but for the renderer rather
than the glyph atlas. Split out so eseq-linux.7 and eseq-linux.8 can be
completed and closed by a Linux-only worker.

THE ORDERING IS THE WHOLE POINT: you cannot capture a wgpu-vs-Metal
comparison before the wgpu side renders. So .7 and .8 now own "renders
correctly on Linux, captures produced", and this bead owns "compare against
macOS and sign off". Blocked on both.

WORK:
  1. Pull the pushed eseq-linux branch on the Mac (branch has no upstream yet;
     it must be pushed first).
  2. Run the whole-frame capture path on the Metal backend for the same fixed
     scene set the Linux side captured in .7/.8 -- identical project, window
     size, scale factor, and theme. If the scenes are not pinned to something
     deterministic, this comparison is worthless; verify that before capturing.
  3. Commit the Metal reference PNGs alongside the wgpu ones under the
     crates/eseqlisp/tests/fixtures/ golden subdirectory.
  4. Per-pipeline (8, from .7) and per-widget (25, from .8) diff review.
  5. Sign off, or file specific beads for the widgets/pipelines that differ.

EXPECT AND DO NOT PANIC AT: gamma/colorspace differences, and MSL-vs-WGSL
float precision divergence. Neither is a per-widget bug -- if a constant
offset shows up across ALL captures, that is one systemic colorspace or
sRGB-surface-format issue, not 25 shader bugs. Diagnose the systemic case
first before opening per-widget beads, or you will file two dozen duplicates
of the same root cause.

Record macOS version, chip, and display scale factor in the notes, same as
eseq-linux.24.

title: load_system_ui_font picks a condensed face on Linux (NimbusSansNarrow)
description:
glyph_atlas::load_system_ui_font() has a macOS preference list (SFPro-Regular, .AppleSystemUIFont, Helvetica) and nothing for Linux - it falls straight through to Query{families: [Family::SansSerif]}.

Probed on this box: SizedFontCache::new(1.0) resolves to NimbusSansNarrow-Regular. That is a *condensed* face, so every proportional advance is materially narrower than a normal sans.

This is not just cosmetic. SizedFontCache::measure_text feeds PropTextMeasurer, which is the layout::TextMeasurer the widget layout uses, so label widths, alignment and cells-per-character estimates all shift. patcher/tests.rs:20605 rendered_label_width_cells is still #[cfg(target_os = "macos")], so nothing guards the Linux value.

Needs a Linux preference list (DejaVu Sans / Noto Sans / Liberation Sans / Cantarell / Inter) before the generic SansSerif fallback.

title: aubio-sys fails to build on Linux (strncasecmp implicit declaration under -std=c99)
description:
`cargo check -p sequencer` fails on Linux: aubio-sys 0.2.1 compiles its vendored aubio C sources with `-std=c99`, which hides POSIX declarations under glibc. `aubio/src/utils/strutils.c:39` then errors with 'implicit declaration of function strncasecmp' (an error, not a warning, under modern GCC/C23 defaults).

Reproduced during review of eseq-linux.4 on Arch (gcc, glibc). macOS is unaffected because Apple libc exposes strncasecmp regardless of the std level.

This blocks building the sequencer crate at all on Linux, so no workspace-wide build or test run is possible there yet.

Options: set CFLAGS/-D_GNU_SOURCE or -std=gnu99 via a build override, patch/vendor aubio-sys, or move to a maintained fork.
acceptance_criteria: cargo check -p sequencer succeeds on Linux

title: Re-vendor DGenLisp from the Linux-ported dgen repo (per-platform binary + toolchain stage)
description:
The sibling dgen repo has a Linux port in good shape and needs to be re-vendored
into this tree so `crates/sequencer/tools/DGenLisp` is usable on Linux.

UPSTREAM (verified 2026-08-23):
  repo   /home/alec/code/dgen-audio   (NOT ~/code/swift/dgen, see below)
  branch linux-c-backend
  HEAD   b053432 "Port DGen to Linux/x86_64 with the C backend"
The port is on a branch with a dirty tree and an untracked Tools/ dir. Confirm
with the dgen agent what the vendorable commit is before pinning; do not vendor
from a dirty working tree.

CURRENT STATE HERE:
- `crates/sequencer/tools/DGenLisp` is git-TRACKED (git ls-files confirms) and
  is a 4.2 MB Mach-O 64-bit arm64 executable. One tracked path cannot be both
  a Mach-O arm64 and an ELF x86_64 binary, so this needs a per-platform
  vendoring layout decision (see below).
- `crates/sequencer/tools/dgen-toolchain/` is the gitignored ~147 MB hermetic
  clang/lld stage; its identity is recorded in the committed
  `content/dgen-toolchain.lock`:
      archive dgen-toolchain-20.1.8-arm64.tar.gz
      archive_sha256 3f5a813d...
      llvm_version 20.1.8 / dgen_abi_version 1
  The lock file has no platform/arch dimension today.

WORK:
1. Layout decision + implementation. Pick one and state why in the bead notes:
   (a) per-platform tracked paths, e.g. tools/DGenLisp-<os>-<arch>, with
       `AppPaths::dgenlisp_tool()` selecting by cfg; or
   (b) stop tracking the binary at all, make it a build/stage artifact like the
       toolchain, gitignored, produced by the rebuild script and pinned in a
       lock file.
   Option (b) is the more honest shape given the toolchain already works that
   way, but it changes fresh-checkout ergonomics — call that out.
2. `AppPaths::dgenlisp_tool()` (crates/sequencer/src/app_paths/mod.rs:119-124)
   currently hardcodes `sequencer_dir.join("tools/DGenLisp")` for Dev and
   `contents_macos.join("DGenLisp")` for Release. Update for the chosen layout.
   The Release arm is macOS-bundle-shaped and Phase 5 says no production code
   constructs it yet — leave it macOS-only rather than inventing a Linux
   bundle layout here.
3. `dgen_toolchain_root_checked()` (mod.rs:165-180) preflights exactly
   `bin/dgen-clang` and `bin/ld64.lld`. `ld64.lld` is the MACH-O linker; a
   Linux stage ships `ld.lld` and emits ELF. Make the expected linker name
   platform-dependent, and keep the existing hard-error-with-hint behavior
   (parent spec Locked Principle 1: no fallback to a system compiler).
4. `rebuild_dgenlisp_tool.sh` at the repo root is macOS-only in three ways:
   - `DGEN_REPO="${DGEN_REPO:-$HOME/code/swift/dgen}"` — a path that does not
     exist on this box; the real repo is ~/code/dgen-audio.
   - `stat -f '%m'` / `stat -f '%Sm %z %N'` are BSD stat; GNU stat needs
     `-c '%Y'` / `-c '%y %s %n'`.
   - it stages `$DGEN_REPO/.toolchain/dgen-toolchain-*.tar.gz` with no arch
     dimension.
   Make the script work on Linux and stage the right archive per host.
5. Extend `content/dgen-toolchain.lock` with a platform/arch dimension (one
   entry per vendored archive) rather than overwriting the arm64 entry.
   Re-vendoring for Linux must NOT invalidate the macOS stage — `--update-lock`
   exists precisely to guard divergence.
6. Verify end to end on Linux: `compile_patch_source_with_dgenlisp`
   (crates/eseqlisp/src/widget_render/patcher/tests.rs:1829) and the
   `lisp_host::dgenlisp_tool_path()` callers actually compile a patch.

side (.dylib -> .so, -shared/-fPIC, ELF audit) is eseq-linux.10, and the
Accelerate/vDSP host-services work is eseq-linux.9. eseq-linux.14 (the
"38 of 41 remaining Linux eseqlisp failures are Exec format error" bead) is
downstream of this one and is now dependent on it: if this lands cleanly those
tests should pass rather than skip.

title: SDF lighting cost: 5x field evaluation per pixel from finite-difference normals
description:
The generated SDF lighting path is the most likely first perf wall on
non-Apple GPUs, and it is fixable entirely in the emitter - no content
changes.

crates/eseqlisp/src/lang/sdf_codegen.rs:640-710 computes the surface normal
by FINITE DIFFERENCES: it evaluates the SDF field at four offset positions
(left, right, up, down) to derive dx/dy, then builds
normalize(float3(dx, dy, 1.0)). So every lit widget evaluates its ENTIRE SDF
expression 5 times per pixel. On top of that, per pixel:
  - 2x normalize (normal, light vector)
  - 2x dot (diffuse, specular)
  - 1x pow() for Blinn-Phong specular (:701-707)

This is not a rare path. content/ui/materials.lisp puts :lighting on
slider-material and slider-material2, so every slider and knob in the UI
pays it.

On Apple silicon this never surfaced (GPU sits ~10%). On an Intel UHD 620 -
roughly 6-8x less ALU, immediate-mode blending instead of TBDR, and DDR4
bandwidth shared with the CPU and the audio engine - this is the term most
likely to dominate.

Options, cheapest first:
  1. Cache the base SDF evaluation and reuse it across the 4 offset taps
     where the expression allows - may cut 5 evaluations toward 4.
  2. Analytic normals for the primitive shapes that have them
     (rounded-rect, circle), falling back to finite differences only for
     arbitrary composed fields.
  3. Replace pow() with a cheaper specular approximation.
  4. A quality tier: emit flat shading (drop :lighting to its :color term)
     under a runtime/backend flag. Lets the Linux target ship before the
     optimization work lands, and gives low-end hardware an escape hatch.

Measure before choosing. Build a shader-cost probe on a representative
sequencer buffer (many sliders and knobs visible) and compare frame time
with lighting on vs forced flat, on BOTH macOS and the UHD 620 box, before
committing to an approach.

Do this work in the emitter so it benefits the Metal target too.
acceptance_criteria: Frame time measured with lighting on vs forced flat on UHD 620; chosen mitigation lands in sdf_codegen.rs and benefits both backends by construction; a flat-shading quality tier exists as a low-end fallback. The macOS half of the frame-time comparison moved to eseq-linux.26.

title: Audio on Linux: verify cpal/ALSA block size, add SCHED_FIFO RT worker priority
description:
Audio is close to free but has two real gaps.

cpal (probably fine): usage is vanilla - crates/sequencer/src/audio/stream.rs
:145 cpal::default_host(), :150 StreamConfig with
:153 BufferSize::Fixed(block_size), f32 output. Dev box confirms ALSA 1.2.16
headers present and PipeWire's pulse server running.
  - VERIFY: BufferSize::Fixed is closer to a suggestion on ALSA than on
    CoreAudio. Confirm the requested block size actually lands, and that the
    audiograph's fixed-block assumptions hold if it does not.
  - Consider enabling cpal's `jack` feature for low latency.
  - Check device enumeration in stream.rs:176-190 (supports_f32 probing)
    behaves sanely against ALSA's virtual devices.

RT thread priority (a real gap): crates/sequencer/audiograph/graph_engine.c
already guards Mach with `#if __has_include(<mach/mach.h>)` (:21), and
crates/sequencer/src/audio/engine.rs:392 sets
`mach_rt_default = cfg!(target_os = "macos") && workers > 0`. So it degrades
SAFELY on Linux - but "degrades" means the audio graph worker threads run at
normal priority and will glitch under load.
  - Add a Linux path: pthread_setschedparam with SCHED_FIFO, mirroring what
    thread_policy_set THREAD_TIME_CONSTRAINT_POLICY does at
    graph_engine.c:579.
  - Needs rtkit (via D-Bus) or a limits.conf rtprio grant; handle the
    permission-denied case gracefully and log it, matching the existing
    WARN at graph_engine.c:584.
  - Wire the existing TINYSEQ_AUDIOGRAPH_MACH_RT env flag (engine.rs:393) or
    introduce a neutral name covering both platforms.
  - graph_engine.c:567 also uses mach_timebase_info for timing; needs a
    clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC) equivalent.
acceptance_criteria: Audio plays on Linux at the requested block size; worker threads acquire RT priority where permitted and log clearly where not; xrun-free under a representative project load

title: dgen dylib pipeline: ELF audit, -shared/-fPIC flags, .dylib -> .so
description:
The dgen compile-and-load pipeline assumes Mach-O, arm64, and .dylib.

1) crates/sequencer/src/lisp_host/dgen/dgen_audit.rs validates every
generated dylib before load:
  :18  use object::read::macho::{LoadCommandVariant, MachHeader}
  :91  MachHeader64::<Endianness>::parse
  :109 checks cputype == CPU_TYPE_ARM64
  :119 checks filetype == MH_DYLIB
  :243 MachOFile64 symbol walk
  :37  hardcodes "/usr/bin/clang"
  :364 test fixtures shell out to /usr/bin/cc with -dynamiclib, -arch arm64,
       -install_name @rpath/{name}.dylib
Needs an ELF sibling. crates/sequencer/Cargo.toml currently enables only the
`macho` feature on the `object` crate - add `elf`. Decide what the Linux
audit actually asserts (ET_DYN, EM_X86_64/EM_AARCH64, DT_NEEDED limited to
libc/libm, no unexpected undefined symbols).

2) Compile flags and naming across lisp_host/dgen/:
  -dynamiclib     -> -shared
  -install_name   -> -soname (or omit)
  -arch arm64     -> drop or map to the host arch
  add -fPIC
  .dylib          -> .so throughout the cache paths
See instrument_compile.rs:373 (dylib_name format), effect_compile.rs:470
(the compile Command), and the dylib_cache module
(lisp_host/dgen/dylib_cache, re-exported at lisp_host/mod.rs:58).

3) There are ~30 dylib_cache.acquire() call sites in app/edit.rs,
app/effects.rs, app/fx_chain.rs - they should not need changes if the naming
is centralized, but verify.

dlopen/dlclose semantics themselves are fine on Linux. Watch for
RTLD_LOCAL/RTLD_GLOBAL differences on hot-swap and for symbol interposition
behaving differently than on macOS two-level namespaces.

Related: the eseq-toolchain epic.
acceptance_criteria: A lisp DSP source compiles to a .so, passes an ELF audit, dlopens, and produces audio on Linux; hot-swap works across reloads; macOS path unchanged

title: dgen host services: drop Accelerate/vDSP (4 symbols) for a portable FFT
description:
crates/sequencer/build.rs unconditionally emits
`cargo:rustc-link-lib=framework=Accelerate`, and
crates/sequencer/audiograph/dgen_host_services.c:14 does
`#include <Accelerate/Accelerate.h>`. Neither exists on Linux.

Good news: the vDSP surface is narrow. Only 4 symbols across 11 call sites:
  vDSP_create_fftsetup
  vDSP_fft_zip
  vDSP_zvma
  vDSP_Length

The DGen ABI v1 host-services table is vDSP-backed; generated DGen dylibs
themselves stay libSystem-only and never link Accelerate, so this is
confined to the host.

Scope:
- Replace the FFT with a portable implementation (kissfft or pffft vendored
  into audiograph/, or expose rustfft through the host-services table -
  rustfft 6.2 is already a sequencer dependency).
- Replace vDSP_zvma (complex vector multiply-add) - trivial to hand-write.
- Make the Accelerate link in build.rs conditional on target_os = macos.
- Keep the ABI v1 host-services table layout byte-identical so existing
  generated dylibs stay valid.

Also confirm the split-radix / packed-complex convention vDSP_fft_zip uses
matches whatever replaces it - this is the classic place to silently get
scaling or bin ordering wrong. Add a numeric test comparing outputs before
switching macOS over.

Related: the eseq-toolchain epic covers shipping the embedded dgen toolchain.
acceptance_criteria: audiograph builds and links on Linux with no Accelerate; numeric test shows the replacement FFT matches vDSP output within tolerance; ABI v1 host-services table layout unchanged

title: Port 25 widget fragment shaders to WGSL (~2165 lines)
description:
Port the per-widget fragment shaders to WGSL. ~2,165 lines of MSL across 25
widget modules in crates/eseqlisp/src/widget_render/. Depends on
eseq-linux.2 (backend-tagged trait) and the WIDGET_SHADER_PREAMBLE port in
eseq-linux.7, since each of these is concatenated onto that preamble.

By MSL volume:
  sound_glyph 364, mod 247, button 224, response_curve_editor 158,
  adsr_editor 158, matrix 128, phaser_notch 126, modulator_curve 87,
  knob_number 84, roar_shaper 80, multiband_meter 64, roar_filter 63,

work the SDF DSL can already express. Where that is true, consider deleting

maintaining two translations. Evaluate per widget; do not force it.

The per-widget pixel diff vs macOS is NOT part of this bead -- it is eseq-linux.25.

title: Port the 8 core MSL pipelines in metal_backend.rs to WGSL (~1150 lines)
description:
Port the 8 hand-written MSL pipelines in crates/eseqlisp/src/ui/metal_backend.rs
to WGSL. ~1,149 lines of MSL. Mechanical but real.

  :100  SHADER_SRC                    text quad (vert + frag)
  :147  PROP_FRAG_SRC                 proportional text fragment
  :171  IMAGE_SHADER_SRC              image_vert / image_frag
  :247  PATCH_CABLE_SHADER_SRC        patch_cable_vert (:292) / frag (:467)
  :513  WIDGET_SHADER_PREAMBLE        instance struct, varyings, SDF utils
  :572  DEFAULT_WIDGET_VERTEX_SHADER  widget_vert
  :762  WAVETABLE_SHADER_SRC          wavetable_vert / wavetable_frag
  :924  WAVEFORM_SHADER_SRC           waveform_vert / waveform_frag
  :1170 LIVE_SPECTROGRAM_SHADER_SRC   live_spectrogram_vert / frag

Plus crates/eseqlisp/shaders/button_surface.metal (96 lines), the only
standalone .metal file.

The WIDGET_SHADER_PREAMBLE is the important one - it defines the shared
WidgetInstance struct, WidgetVaryings, and the SDF utility functions that
every per-widget fragment shader (eseq-linux.8) is concatenated onto. Port
it first and get it right.

Known translation hazards beyond type renames:
- WGSL has no implicit numeric conversions; MSL mixes int/float freely.
- [[stage_in]] / [[buffer(n)]] / [[vertex_id]] / [[instance_id]] ->
  @location / @group+@binding / @builtin.
- Texture sampling model differs substantially (separate sampler objects).
- MSL fast-math and half precision defaults may be silently relied on.
  Expect "compiles fine, renders differently" on a subset.

Suggested order: text quad first (proves the glyph atlas end to end), then

title: [macOS host] Verification riders sweep: darwin cargo check, clipping tests, macOS frame times
description:
REQUIRES A MACOS MACHINE. A batching bead: four separate beads each carry one
small macOS-only verification clause. Rather than stranding four Linux beads
on a host they cannot reach, each keeps its Linux-verifiable acceptance and
hands its macOS rider here, so one Mac session clears all of them.

Pull the pushed eseq-linux branch and run:

  1. From eseq-linux.22 -- `cargo check` clean on x86_64-apple-darwin (and
     aarch64-apple-darwin if that is the real target; .22 names x86_64, which
     is worth double-checking against what you actually ship, since the
     vendored DGenLisp is arm64). Cross-checking darwin from Linux needs the
     macOS SDK, which is why it cannot be done on the worker host.
  2. From eseq-linux.17 -- the existing macOS clipping tests still pass after
     the scissor/clip math is shared with ui::gpu_geometry.
  3. From eseq-linux.13 -- macOS frame time with SDF lighting on vs forced
     flat. The Linux/UHD 620 half is measured by the worker; this supplies the
     macOS half of that comparison.
  4. From eseq-linux.12 -- confirm the macOS-gated tests the worker triaged
     are genuinely macOS-only and still pass on a Mac, rather than having been
     gated to hide a real cross-platform failure. This is the one with actual
     judgement in it -- a test gated `#[cfg(target_os = "macos")]` during a
     port is exactly where a genuine bug gets quietly buried.

Item 4 is the reason this bead is worth doing rather than skipping. Items 1-3
are mechanical.

Do not start until the depended-on beads have landed their Linux halves;
otherwise there is nothing to verify.

title: Post-CoreText cleanup: dead objc2 deps, stale comments, warn spam
description:
Loose ends left by 57b76e2a. All verified by grep over crates/:

1. objc2-core-graphics (Cargo.toml:50-55, features CGBitmapContext/CGColorSpace/CGContext/CGImage) is now entirely unused - zero references to objc2_core_graphics::, CGBitmapContext, CGColorSpace, CGContext, CGGlyph or CGImage remain. Drop the dependency.
2. objc2-core-foundation still enables features CFAttributedString and CFDictionary (Cargo.toml:48); the only remaining use is objc2_core_foundation::CGSize at metal_backend.rs:21. Trim the feature list.
3. widget_render/patcher/display.rs:310 still explains a constant in terms of CoreText measurements. Reword for the portable path.
4. glyph_atlas.rs:239 eprintln fires whenever the resolved PostScript name differs from the requested string. Resolution via the family-name branch always trips that, so a correct resolution warns - and it warns again on every atlas rebuild. Warn only when the fallback is genuine.
5. glyph_atlas.rs:246 calls font.rasterize('m', size) purely to read advance_width and discards the bitmap; font.metrics('m', size) gives the same number without rasterizing.
6. load_font and load_named_font duplicate the same with_face_data / Font::from_bytes / FontSettings block; factor it out (folds naturally into the caching in eseq-linux.21).
acceptance_criteria: unused dependency and features removed; cargo check clean on Linux; stale CoreText comment reworded; warn fires only on genuine fallback. The x86_64-apple-darwin cross-check moved to eseq-linux.26 (needs the macOS SDK).

title: Atlas rebuild re-copies and re-parses the whole font file on every text-zoom step
description:
glyph_atlas::load_named_font / load_font call db.with_face_data(...) and then Font::from_bytes(data.to_vec(), ...) - a full heap copy of the font file plus a full fontdue parse, every time.

metal_backend.rs:3767 rebuilds text_atlas whenever |text_atlas_zoom - zoom| > 0.001, i.e. on every zoom step, and :6119-:6135 builds three atlases (atlas, text_atlas, prop_atlas) on scale change. JetBrains Mono Nerd Font is roughly 4 MB, so that is ~12 MB of copying and three parses per rebuild.

The old CoreText path was effectively free here - CTFont::with_name hits the system font cache.

Cache the parsed fontdue::Font (or at least the face bytes) keyed by face id; fontdue::Font is size-independent, so one parse can serve every size and zoom level.
acceptance_criteria: rebuilding the text atlas at a new zoom does not re-read or re-parse font file bytes

title: Share the scissor/clip math with metal_backend.rs instead of two copies
description:
eseq-linux.5 introduced ui::gpu_geometry::{ScissorRect, ClipStack} for the wgpu backend, but metal_backend.rs still carries its own intersect_scissor_rects (:9562) and scissor_segments walk over MTLScissorRect. The two now compute the same clip-stack intersection independently and can drift.

Convert the Metal path to build ScissorRect via the shared helpers and convert to MTLScissorRect only at the encoder boundary. This is a Metal-side change, so it needs a macOS machine to test - it was deliberately left out of eseq-linux.5, which could only be verified on Linux.
acceptance_criteria: metal_backend.rs no longer defines its own scissor intersection; both backends derive clip rects from ui::gpu_geometry; Linux-runnable clipping tests pass and the macOS-only clipping tests are left untouched and compile-checked as far as Linux allows. Running the macOS clipping tests moved to eseq-linux.26.

title: ui::theme tests race on the process-global ACTIVE_THEME
description:
`ui::theme::tests::theme_slot_overrides_apply_to_named_colors` (theme.rs:~1180) calls `sync_from_value` to swap every theme slot, then restores it with `set_current`. `ACTIVE_THEME` is a process-global RwLock, so while that body runs every concurrently-scheduled test that reads `theme::current()` sees the override colours.

Observed: `ui::theme::tests::agentic_bubble_slots_round_trip_through_a_theme_override` fails intermittently in a full `cargo test -p eseqlisp --lib` run (2 of 4 runs at 7f580a54, i.e. pre-existing, not caused by eseq-linux.3). eseq-linux.3's shader golden test hit the same race and was fixed by threading an explicit theme instead (commit 6a5fb546) - the theme tests themselves still race.

Fix options: serialise the theme-mutating tests behind a shared mutex, or make them operate on an explicit `Theme` value rather than the global.
acceptance_criteria: A full cargo test -p eseqlisp --lib run passes the ui::theme tests repeatedly (>=5 consecutive runs) with no theme-related intermittent failures

title: Linux validation: iGPU perf budget, full test suite green, CI target
description:
Confirm the renderer is actually usable on non-Apple hardware, and that the
whole workspace builds and tests green on Linux.

Perf reality check. The dev box is an Intel UHD 620 (Kaby Lake-R). eseq's
renderer is tuned for Apple GPUs - see UI_PERFORMANCE_TUNING.md. SDF-heavy
fragment shaders with per-widget instancing is a different regime on a weak
iGPU with shared memory bandwidth.
  - The retained primitive-run cache has to be genuinely effective, not just
    present: WIDGET_PRIMITIVE_CACHE (widget_render/mod.rs:245),
    MetalPrimitiveRunIndex (:806), RetainedMetalPrimitiveRunStats (:814).
    Instrument reuse rate on Linux.
  - `vulkaninfo` is not installed on the dev box; confirm mesa's vulkan-intel
    is present or wgpu silently falls back to GL with different perf and
    feature characteristics. Log and assert the chosen wgpu backend at
    startup.
  - Establish a frame-time budget on the reference project and treat
    regressions against it as bugs.

Build and test. Get the full workspace green:
  cargo nextest run  (see CLAUDE.md for the test stack budget - 16 MiB
  RUST_MIN_STACK from .cargo/config.toml, and the disposable worktree
  recipe for clean-HEAD checks)
Baseline as of 2026-08-20 on macOS: 4,272 passed / 32 skipped debug,
4,270 / 32 release, per docs/test-suite-performance.md.
  - crates/sequencer/src/ui/state_values/tests.rs has ~12 cfg(target_os="macos")
    gated tests, and widget_render/patcher/tests.rs (49) and editor/tests.rs
    (48) have many more. Decide per test: genuinely macOS-specific, or just
    gated because the primitive IR was gated (eseq-linux.1 should free most
    of these).
  - Add Linux to CI so the port does not rot.
acceptance_criteria: Full workspace test suite passes on Linux; every test skipped or gated for Linux is enumerated with a stated reason (not silently gated); wgpu backend selection asserted at startup; frame-time budget recorded for the reference project on UHD 620; Linux job added to CI. Confirming the gated tests still pass on a Mac moved to eseq-linux.26.
notes:
Linux baseline measured 2026-08-23, right after eseq-linux.1 + its review fixes (commit 9354350d). 'cargo test -p eseqlisp --lib': 1635 passed / 41 failed / 3 ignored. Breakdown of the 41:
  - 38: DGenLisp is a Mach-O arm64 binary, 'Exec format error' -> eseq-linux.14
  - 2: geometry that depends on real text measurement, so the terminal
       chars().count() fallback gives different node widths --
       patcher_alignment_snaps_dragged_output_to_other_input_x and

  - 3: pass in isolation, fail under nextest/test parallelism (shared global
